subject: Request: temporary HC bridge & review-contingent backfill
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary HC bridge & review-contingent backfill

Team —

Quick summary: an unexpected resignation hit my team yesterday (IC on Platform Reliability) and the person will be off in six weeks. This role is mid-cycle for performance calibration and we have a high-impact migration in May that we cannot absorb without coverage.

As discussed in the org-planning forum, there's a hiring freeze in effect through Q2 except for approved freeze exceptions. I'm requesting a temporary HC bridge (3 months, contractor or temp-to-perm) while we finish the performance review cycle and confirm any permanent backfill. Rationale and tradeoffs attached (hc_tradeoff_rationale_v1.pdf).

Proposed ask:
- Freeze-exception approval for 1 headcount (3 months) to hire a contractor or a temp-to-perm through HireRight.
- Contingency: if performance reviews result in reallocation (promotion/internal move), we will cancel the external backfill and redeploy budget. If we do hire permanent, we will follow standard requisition + recruiting.

Why this is urgent:
- The migration in May requires 40% of the outgoing IC's capacity for two sprints.
- Without coverage we risk delaying launch and incurring higher runbook toil.

Budget note: I modeled costs in the attached mutual_action_plan.xlsx; this uses existing discretionary runway for the 3-month window.

Can Marissa/Laur a confirm what documentation you need for the freeze exception and whether Finance is comfortable with the proposed 3-month contingency? Karthik — can you confirm the SRE oncall rotation impact if we don't get this approved?

Thanks —
Logan
---
Logan Wright
Staff Engineering Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary HC bridge & review-contingent backfill

Logan — thanks for the clear write-up and attachments. A few quick items I need before I can route a formal freeze-exception: 

1) Confirmation of exact scope & hours for the contractor (FTE equivalence).
2) Timeline we want the contractor onboarded by (recruiting lead time).
3) A note from Finance that the discretionary fund covers this (Laura — can you confirm or flag).
4) A proposed acceptance criteria for canceling the external hire if an internal reallocation happens (so we can include it in the exception docs).

If you can get those to me by end of day Monday I can push a formal request to People Ops and Legal next morning. The exception typically requires VP-level signoff if cost > $Xk over three months — I'll include the minimal approver list once I have the numbers.

Marissa
---
Marissa Cole
Head of People Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary HC bridge & review-contingent backfill

Thanks for the heads-up, Logan — I reviewed the mutual_action_plan.xlsx and the preliminary cost model looks reasonable for a 3-month bridge. We can fund a contractor from discretionary budget but need the following to sign off: 

- A one-page budget memo that calls out total expected cost, GL code to charge, and owner for cost tracking.
- A clear cancellation clause that zeroes the commitment if an internal reallocation occurs post-review.
- Recruiter/vendor selection (HireRight OK as a vendor but we need vendor PO language; Procurement will handle).

If you provide the memo and acceptance criteria, I'll route Finance approval by end of day Monday. Once Finance signs, Marissa can submit to Legal for the exception paperwork.

One quick note on timing: recruiting + background typically takes 3 weeks, so target onboarding by 10 May to meet the migration ramp.

Laura
---
Laura Bennett
Finance Business Partner, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, HireRight Talent <sarah@hireright.co>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@example.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary HC bridge & review-contingent backfill

Appended: one-page budget memo and proposed cancellation criteria (attached: hc_tradeoff_rationale_v1.pdf and performance_summary_q1.pdf). Summary below for convenience: 

- Total expected cost (3 months contractor): $42,500 (includes onboarding fees). GL code: 5200-Infra-Eng. Owner: Logan Wright.
- Onboard target: 2027-05-10 (recruiting initiated today with HireRight).
- Cancellation criteria: if post-review (by 2027-05-30) an internal reallocation or promotion covers >=60% of role capacity for at least two successive sprints, we will cancel contractor engagement and stop further spend.

Karthik: the SRE rotation impact if we don't get coverage is an extra oncall person for two sprints and additional nightly pager noise; I documented the mitigation plan in the attachment.

Next steps: Marissa to route freeze-exception with attachments and Laura to confirm Finance sign-off. Recruiter (Sarah) — please confirm candidate shortlist ETA (Cc'd).

Thanks everyone — will update the thread as approvals land.

Logan
